The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that, on 02.07.2021 at about 11.00 a.m., when the petitioner was riding Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KL-1600 proceeding from Bettahalli towards Kadabagere Piple Line Road, Dasanapura Hobli,
Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that time the rider of another Honda Activa motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029 came from opposite direction in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life came to the extreme wrong side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's Honda Activa.
Due to impact petitioner fell down along with the vehicle and sustained fracture injuries.

Immediately, after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Anupama Hospital, Byadarahalli Magadi Main Road for treatment, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 02.07.2021 to 07.07.2021 i.e., for a period of 6 days, wherein Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75669137/
2

sentences.text: petitioner underwent CT abdomen and pelvis done, MRI of spine was done and was kept in ICU SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.983/2022 for observation and still he is under treatment and discharged with an advise to take followup treatment.

The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
3.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, running shop in the name and style as Sri Sai Vijayaraja Traders and also the owner of the said firm.

He was also dealer in wholesale water purifier, water heater, chimney, geyser etc., and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/-
per month.

The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of the Honda Activa Scooter,
bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029 by its rider and in this connection the Madanayakanahalli Police have registered a case in their crime No.0335/2021, after investigation the said police have filed charge sheet against the said rider for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC R/w Sec.134 (a) & (b) of MV Act.
The first respondent being the Insurer and the second respondent being the RC Owner of offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.983/2022 and severally liable for payment of compensation.
4. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 before the Court through its counsel and filed its written statement.
The Respondent No.2 remained absent and hence was placed exparte.
5. Respondent No.1 has filed its objection contending that the claim petition is false and petition is not maintainable.
Further contended that, the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Respondent has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of Honda Activa motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029 and the liability if any, shall be strictly subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the petitioner has to put strict proof of the same.
The alleged accident is caused solely due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Further contended that there was a delay of one day in filing the complaint the reason for delay in the lodging the complaint is not properly explained.

It has also contended that the Honda SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.983/2022 Activa motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029 was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and with the Police, only in order to get higher compensation.

sentences.text: It has further contended as per the MLC of Anupama Hospital, the history of accident is mentioned as "Skid & Fall from two wheeler" and has given the statement that the alleged history of RTA, patient was rider of the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KL-1660 hit by another two wheeler i.e., Honda Activa motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029 - these facts clearly shows that the petitioner by suppressing the material facts cooked up a false story of involvement of the insured vehicle in the alleged accident though it was not at all involved.
The petition is a bad for non-joinder of necessary party as such the owner and insurer of the TP motor cycle were not made as parties to the proceedings.
It has also contended at the time of alleged accident the petitioner was not wearing helmet and thereby violated Sec.129 of MV Act.

Further contended that the rider of the Honda SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.983/2022 Activa motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029 was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75669137/
3 accident.

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent knowing fully well that the rider of the motor cycle was not having valid and effective DL will fully entrusted his vehicle to the said rider and thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed:
:: ISSUES::
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 02.07.2021 at about 11.00 a.m., he was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing Reg.no.KA- 05-KL-16000 from Bettahalli to Kadabagere Pipe Line Road and at that time, a motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029 being ridden by its rider at high speed in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed against his motor cycle, as a result, he fell on the ground and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.983/2022 2. What petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition? If so, from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award ?
7.
The petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
He has examined Lohith Gowda/ Medical Record Officer of Anumpama Hospital as PW.2 and got marked 6 documents as Ex.P11 to 16.

On the other hand,
Legal Executive of 1st respondent insurance company have examined themselves as RW1 & RW2 and got marked Ex.R1 & Ex.R2 and closed their side.
8. Heard the arguments from both side.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has filed its citation in MFA No.4407/2020 (MV-D) C/w MFA No.4081/2020 (MV- D).
Perused the entire records.

9. My answers to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.983/2022 Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75669137/
4  REASONS 10. Issue No.1:

entities.text: Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW- 1.
He has got marked 10 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.10.
He has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed for his examination- in-chief.

11. It is relevant to note that the respondent No.1 has specifically contended that, the motor cycle bearing No.KA- 51 EU-6029 was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with owner of the vehicle.
Further contended that As per MLC of Anupama Hospital, the History mentioned as Skid and fall from two wheeler and compliant lodged after one day of accident.

Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of rider of Active motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU-6029.
12.

Petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and in his evidence has stated that on 02.07.2021 at about 11.00 a.m., when the petitioner was riding Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KL-1600 proceeding from Betthalli towards SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.983/2022 Kadabagere Piple Line Road,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that time the rider of another Honda Activa motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51- EU-6029 came from opposite direction in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life came to the extreme wrong side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's Honda Activa.
Due to impact petitioner fell down along with the vehicle and sustained fracture injuries.

13. PW.1 in support of his version, he has produced the certified copy of FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, IMV report, wound certificate and final report and got them marked at Ex.P1 to 6.
14.

I have perused Ex.P1 to 6, from these documents it is clear that, the accident took place on 02-07-2021 at about 11.00a.m pm., and the FIR at Ex.P1 in crime No.335/2021 came to be registered on 03-07-2021 at around 8.20p.m, at Maadanayakanahally Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.

Ex.P2 - Complaint was lodged by one Smt. Jaisheela, Ex.P3 - Spot SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.983/2022 Panchanama describe the place of accident, Ex.P4 - IMV report reveals that front shape left side scratched and also reveals that the incident is not due to the any mechanical defects.

Thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet at Ex.P.6 against the rider of the alleged motor cycle bearing No.KA-51 EU-6029 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
15.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW1.
PW1 denied that the injury sustained by him due to his negligence and self-fall from bike due to skid and fall.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

5 16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent No.1 argued that as per MLC EX.P-12 and case sheet EX.P-16, it is clearly shows that the accident occurred is only negligence of the petitioner due to self-fall from bike to skid and fall SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.983/2022 and respondent No.1 and offending motorcycle is falsely implicated in this petition for getting the compensation.
The respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation to petitioner and also relied the judgment of the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.4407/2020 (MV-D) C/w MFA No.4081/2020 (MV-D).
Perused the EX.P-12 MLC extract, it shows that it R/T/A self fall from bike due to skid and fall @ 11.00 am toady near Kadabagere.

During the investigation, Ex.P-14 and Ex.P-15 is shows that,
according to the statemnt given by patient A/H/o RTA, patient was rider of 2 wheelar No.KA 05/KL1600 hit by another 2 wheeler No. KA- 51 Eu-6029 on 02-07-2021 at around 11.00 a.m., at Near Bettahalli to Kadabagere pipeline road Dasanapura (H) Bangalore sustained injury to lowback.
As per records, EX.P-12 MLC intimation to the police for information of Smt.Jasisheela, who is the sister of the petitioner.
The Said Smt Jaisheela was a not eye witness of the accident.
During the investigation, in the statement of petitioner/injured , it is found that the accident occurred in offending motorcycle bearing KA-51 EU-6029.
Therefore facts and circumstance SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.983/2022 of the case, the decision relied by the respondent No.1 is not applicable to the case on hand.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of rider of the offending motor cycle which belongs to the respondent No.2.

Accordingly,
I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.2:-

The specific contention of the petitioner is that, he was riding Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-05-KL-1600 proceeding from Bettahalli towards Kadabagere Piple Line Road, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that time the rider of another Honda Activa motor cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EU- 6029 came from opposite direction in high speed, in a rash SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.983/2022 and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life came to the extreme wrong side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's Honda Activa.
Due to impact petitioner fell down along with the vehicle and sustained fracture injuries.
18. Immediately after the accident he was shifted to the Anupama hospital and he has taken treatment in the said hospital as an inpatient from 02-07-2021 to 07-07- 2021.
The petitioner has produced the medical documents to support of his case i.e., wound certificate as per Ex.P.5 and discharge summary as per Ex.P.7.

On perusal of Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.7, it disclose that, the petitioner has sustained injury of Burst fracture D12 vertebral body with retropusion causing Mild to moderate spinal canal stenosis, T2 & STIR Hyperintensity in thoracic spinal cord at D12 vertebral level- cord contusion/Edema and Pain at injured site and C/o numbers of both lower limbs in the said accident.
The said injuires are grievous in nature.
Therefore, on perusal of the Ex.P.5, it discloses that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
The petitioner has contended that, he has made expenses of Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.983/2022 nourishment and other incidental charges

Therefore on perusal of these medical records disclose that, the petitioner has sustained injury in the road traffic accident which has been occurred on due to rash and Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75669137/
6

entities.text: Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: negligent driving of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51 EU-6029, which proved by the petitioner in issue No.1.
Therefore, the petitioner is sustained injury in the said accident.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation on the following heads.
19. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:

As per the Wound certificate and discharge summary produced at Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.7, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries i.e, Burst fracture D12 vertebral body with retropusion causing Mild to moderate spinal canal stenosis, T2 & STIR Hyperintensity in thoracic spinal cord at D12 vertebral level- cord contusion/Edema and Pain at injured site and C/o numbers of both lower limbs.
The doctor has opined that, the injuries are grievous in nature and the same is mentioned in Ex.P.5.
The discharge summary issued by the Anupama hospital, discloses that, the petitioner was treated as an inpatient from 02-07-2021 to 07-07-2021.
The SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.983/2022 petitioner has not examined the doctor and there is no disability certificate.

As per guidelines issued by the Central Government for the purpose of assessing the extent of specified disability in a person included under the rights of persons with disability Act 2016 dated 04-01-2018, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not come under the any disability.

entities.text: rights of persons with disability Act 2016
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the injuries sustained by the petitioner do not cause any disability for the petitioner's body or part of the body.
However, in view of the injury sustained by him in the accident he had suffered pain.
Therefore, he is entitled for sum amount of compensation for pain and suffering.

Therefore, by considering the above facts and looking to the nature of injuries and considering age and status of the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and sufferings.
20. LOSS OF AMENITIES:

Further on perusal of evidence of PW-1, it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained Burst fracture D12 vertebral body with retropusion causing Mild to moderate spinal canal SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.983/2022 stenosis, T2 & STIR Hyperintensity in thoracic spinal cord at D12 vertebral level-cord contusion/Edema and Pain at injured site and C/o numbers of both lower limbs.
The petitioner was aged about 34 years and he is working wholesale dealer of Purifier solar water heater, chimney, Geezer etc at the time of accident.
Though the petitioner is earning member and he lost his business.
Therefore, he has lost business during the treatment period.

By considering the above facts and circumstances and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.
21. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner has got marked the document as per Ex.P.8 i.e., medical bills in 21 Nos.
The petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient from 02-07- 2021 to 07-07-2021 i.e., 2 days.
The total medical bills is of Rs.60,125/-.

The respondents have not disputed the medical bills produced by the petitioner except denial during the course of cross-examination of the PW-1 as the SCCH - 26 18 MVC No.983/2022 petitioner has not made such expenses for his medical treatment.
But Ex.P.8 is issued by the hospital as they have received the such bill under Ex.P.8.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for medical bills covered under Ex.P.11 i.e., Rs.60,125/-.
Hence, I proceed to award Rs.60,125/- under the head of medical expenses.
22. ATTENDANT, FOOD AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Further on perusal of Ex-P-7 i.e.,
discharge summary, it shows that, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 02-07-2021 to 07-07-2021 for a period of 6 days.

Looking to the period of hospitalization and the Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75669137/
7 petitioner required to take assistance of another as his attender during the treatment period and for such period they have to made expenses for food and other conveyance.

entities.text: Nagesh.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.9,000/- under the head of attendant, food and conveyance charges.
23. The petitioner contended that, he has lost for 6 months his business.

But when he comes to oral evidence, SCCH - 26 19 MVC No.983/2022 he has filed examination in chief on affidavit and he has also stated in the evidence as there is a loss of his business,but no document is produced for his loss of business.
The injuries are not amount to any disability under the guidelines issued by the central government in the year 2018.

Therefore, by considering the all these aspects the petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable compensation under the following heads:-
Compensation heads
Compensation amount 1. Towards Pain and Rs. 30,000/- Sufferings 2. Towards loss of Rs. 20,000/- Amenities 3. Towards Medical Rs. 60,125/- Expenses
4.Towards Rs. 9,000/-

Attendant, food and conveyance charges Total Rs. 1,19,125/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,19,125/-.
24. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the SCCH - 26 20 MVC No.983/2022 rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

25. On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of objection statement, it reveal that, the respondent No.2 is the owner and the respondent No.1 is the insurer of the Activa Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-EU-6029.

Further, as stated above that, the alleged accident has been occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the alleged Activa Motor cycle and the policy was in force as on the date of accident and the same has been not disputed by the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of alleged Scorpio Car is liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,19,125/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
26. ISSUE NO.3:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,19,125/- (One Lakh Ninteen Thousand One Hundred Twenty Five Rupees Only) with interest @ 6% p.a, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, in view of the policy, the respondent No.1 insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, looking to the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner,
the entire amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH - 26 22 MVC No.983/2022 Draw award accordingly.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of rider of the offending motor cycle which belongs to the respondent No.2.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation on the following heads.
As per guidelines issued by the Central Government for the purpose of assessing the extent of specified disability in a person included under the rights of persons with disability Act 2016 dated 04-01-2018, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not come under the any disability.
Therefore, the injuries sustained by the petitioner do not cause any disability for the petitioner's body or part of the body.
However, in view of the injury sustained by him in the accident he had suffered pain.
Therefore, he is entitled for sum amount of compensation for pain and suffering.
